exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Tangental Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity

question.text: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) = \langle \sin{t}, \, 2,\, \cos{t} \rangle.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by \[ a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(\sin{t} \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 2 \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(\cos{t}) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \cos{t}, \, 0, \, -\sin{t} \right\rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a$ and $||\mathbf v||\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a & = \left\langle \sin{t}, \, 2, \, \cos{t} \right\rangle \cdot \left\langle \cos{t}, \, 0,\, -\sin{t} \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \sin{t}\cos{t} + 0 - \cos{t}\sin{t},\\[3pt] & = 0,\\[7pt] ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{ \left( \sin{t} \right)^2 + \left( 2 \right)^2 + \left( \cos{t} \right)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{\sin^2{t} + \cos^2{t} + 4}\\[3pt] & = \sqrt{1 + 4}\\[3pt] & = \sqrt{5} \end{align}

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_T & = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{0}{\sqrt{5}}\\[5pt] & = 0. \end{align}

question.text: The position $\mathbf r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf r(t) = \left\langle \sqrt{3}t , \, t^2, \, t+1 \right\rangle.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by \[ a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf v & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(\sqrt{3}t\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(t^2\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(t+1\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \sqrt{3}, \, 2t,\, 1 \right\rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( \sqrt{3} \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 2t \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 1 \right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 0, \, 2,\, 0 \right\rangle \end{align}

Then, we compute $\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a$ and $||\mathbf v||\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a & = \left\langle \sqrt{3}, \, 2t, \, 1 \right\rangle \cdot \left\langle 0, \, 2,\, 0 \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = 4t \\[6pt] ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{ \left(\sqrt{3}\right)^2 + \left(2t\right)^2 + \left(1\right)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{4 + 4t^2} \\[3pt] & = 2\sqrt{1 + t^2} \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_T & = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{4t}{2\sqrt{1 + t^2}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2t}{\sqrt{1 + t^2}}. \end{align}

question.text: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) = \langle e^t, \, -2e^{-2t},\, 1 \rangle.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by \[ a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(e^t\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-2e^{-2t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(1) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle e^t, \, 4e^{-2t},\, 0 \right\rangle \\[3pt] \end{align} \]

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a$ and $||\mathbf v||\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a & = \left\langle e^t, \, -2e^{-2t},\, 1 \right\rangle \cdot \left\langle e^t, \, 4e^{-2t},\, 0 \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = e^{2t} -8e^{-4t},\\[6pt] ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{ \left(e^t\right)^2 +\left(2e^{-2t}\right)^2 + 1^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{e^{2t}+4e^{-4t}+ 1}. \end{align}

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_T & = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{e^{2t} -8e^{-4t}}{ \sqrt{e^{2t}+4e^{-4t}+ 1}}. \end{align}

question.text: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) = \langle t^2, \, 1,\, 3t \rangle.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by \[ a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(t^2\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 1 \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(3t) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 2t, \, 0, \, 3 \right\rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a$ and $||\mathbf v||\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a & = \left\langle t^2, \, 1, \, 3t \right\rangle \cdot \left\langle 2t, \, 0,\, 3 \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = 2t^3 + 9t\\[5pt] & = t(2t^2 + 9),\\[7pt] ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{ \left( t^2 \right)^2 + \left( 1 \right)^2 + \left( 3t \right)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{t^4 + 9t^2 + 1}\\[3pt] \end{align}

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_T & = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] % & = \dfrac{2t^3 + 9t}{\sqrt{t^4 + 9t^2 + 1}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{t(2t^2 + 9)}{\sqrt{t^4 + 9t^2 + 1}}. \end{align}

question.text: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t > 0$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) = \langle \sqrt{6t}, \, 3,\, -t \rangle.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by \[ a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(\sqrt{6t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 3 \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(-t) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6t}}, \, 0, \, -1 \right\rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a$ and $||\mathbf v|| {:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a & = \left\langle \sqrt{6t}, \, 3, \, -t \right\rangle \cdot \left\langle \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6t}}, \, 0,\, -1 \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = t + 3,\\[7pt] ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{ \left( \sqrt{6t} \right)^2 + \left( 3 \right)^2 + \left( -t \right)^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{t^2 + 6t + 9}\\[5pt] & = \sqrt{(t + 3)^2}\\[5pt] & = t + 3 \end{align}

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_T & = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{t+3}{t+3}\\[5pt] & = 1. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Normal Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity

question.text: The position $\mathbf r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t > 0$ is given by $\mathbf r(t)= \left\langle \dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{t^3}, \, 4t,\, -7 \right\rangle.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The normal component of acceleration is given by \[ a_N = \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||} \]

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: \begin{align} \mathbf v & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( \dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{t^3} \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 4t \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( -7 \right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \sqrt{t}, \, 4, \, 0 \right\rangle \end{align}

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( \sqrt{t} \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 4 \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 0 \right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}, \, 0, \, 0 \right\rangle \end{align}

Now, we compute $\mathbf v \times \mathbf a, ||\mathbf v||$ and $||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v \times \mathbf a & = \left\langle \sqrt{t}, \, 4, \, 0 \right\rangle \times \left\langle \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}, \, 0, \, 0 \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \begin{array}{|ccc|} \mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ \sqrt{t} & 4 & 0 \\ \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0 & 0 \end{array} \\[5pt] & = \ \begin{array}{|cc|} 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{array} \, \mathbf{i} - \begin{array}{|cc|} \sqrt{t} & 0 \\ \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0 \end{array} \, \mathbf{j} + \begin{array}{|cc|} \sqrt{t} & 4 \\[0pt] \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0 \end{array} \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 0 , 0 , -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{t}} \right\rangle, \\[7pt] ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{\left( \sqrt{t} \right)^2 + \left( 4 \right)^2 + \left( 0 \right)^2}\\[3pt] & = \sqrt{t + 16}, \\[7pt] ||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a|| & = \sqrt{\left(0\right)^2 + \left(0\right)^2 + \left(-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{t}}\right)^2} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{t}} \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_N &= \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}\right)}{\sqrt{t + 16}} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{t(t+16)}}. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Normal Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity

question.text: The position $\mathbf r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf r(t)= \langle t, \, \sin t,\, \cos t \rangle.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The normal component of acceleration is given by \[ a_N = \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||} \]

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf v & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(t), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(\sin t), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(\cos t) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle 1, \, \cos t,\, -\sin t \rangle \\[3pt] \end{align} \]

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(1), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(\cos t), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(-\sin t) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle 0, \, -\sin t,\, -\cos t \rangle. \end{align}

Now, we compute $\mathbf v \times \mathbf a, ||\mathbf v||$ and $||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v \times \mathbf a & = \langle 1, \, \cos t,\, -\sin t \rangle \times \langle 0, \, -\sin t,\, -\cos t \rangle \\[3pt] & = \begin{array}{|ccc|} \mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & \cos t & -\sin t \\ 0 & -\sin{t} & -\cos t \end{array} \\[5pt] & = \ \begin{array}{|cc|} \cos t & -\sin t \\ -\sin{t} & -\cos t \end{array} \, \mathbf{i} - \begin{array}{|cc|} 1 & -\sin t \\ 0 & -\cos t \end{array} \, \mathbf{j} + \begin{array}{|cc|} 1& \cos t \\ 0 & -\sin{t} \end{array} \, \mathbf{k} \\[3pt] & = \left\langle (-\cos^2 t - \sin^2 t) , -(-\cos t), (-\sin t) \right\rangle \\[3pt] &= \left\langle -1 , \cos t, -\sin t \right\rangle \\[7pt] ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{1^2 + (\cos t)^2 + (-\sin t)^2}\\[3pt] & = \sqrt{1 + \cos^2 t + \sin^2 t} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{2} \\[7pt] ||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a|| & = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + (\cos t)^2 + (-\sin t)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{1 + \cos^2 t + \sin^2 t} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{2}. \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_N &= \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} \\[5pt] & = 1. \end{align}

question.text: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t > 0$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) = \left\langle t, \, 1, \, \sqrt{2t} \right\rangle.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The normal component of acceleration is given by \[ a_N = \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( t \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 1 \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( \sqrt{2t} \right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 1, \, 0,\, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2t}} \right\rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \times \mathbf a{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v \times \mathbf a & = \left\langle t, \, 1, \, \sqrt{2t} \right\rangle \times \left\langle 1, \, 0,\, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2t}} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \begin{array}{|ccc|} \mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\[5pt] t & 1 & \sqrt{2t} \\[3pt] 1 & 0 & \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2t}} \end{array} \\[5pt] & = \ \begin{array}{|cc|} 1 & \sqrt{2t} \\[3pt] 0 & \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2t}} \end{array} \, \mathbf{i} - \begin{array}{|cc|} t & \sqrt{2t} \\[3pt] 1 & \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2t}} \end{array} \, \mathbf{j} + \begin{array}{|cc|} t & 1 \\[3pt] 1 & 0 \end{array} \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2t}} , \dfrac{\sqrt{2t}}{2}, -1 \right\rangle \end{align}

Now, we compute $||\mathbf v||$ and $||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{\left( t \right)^2 + \left( 1 \right)^2 + \left( \sqrt{2t} \right)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{t^2 + 2t + 1}, \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{(t+1)^2}\\[3pt] & = t+1,\\[7pt] ||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a|| & = \sqrt{\left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2t}} \right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2t}}{2}\right)^2 + \left(-1\right)^2} \\[5pt] & = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2t} + \dfrac{t}{2} + 1} \\[5pt] & = \sqrt{\dfrac{t^2 + 2t + 1}{2t}}\\[5pt] & = \sqrt{\dfrac{(t+1)^2}{2t}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{t+1}{\sqrt{2t}} \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_N &= \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left( \frac{t+1}{\sqrt{2t}} \right)}{t + 1}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}. \end{align}

question.text: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t)= \left\langle \sin{t}, \, -\cos{t},\, 3 \right\rangle.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The normal component of acceleration is given by \[ a_N = \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(\sin{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-\cos{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(3\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle \cos{t}, \, \sin{t},\, 0 \rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \times \mathbf a{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v \times \mathbf a & = \left\langle \sin{t}, \, -\cos{t},\, 3 \right\rangle \times \langle \cos{t}, \, \sin{t},\, 0 \rangle \\[5pt] & = \begin{array}{|ccc|} \mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ \sin{t} & -\cos{t} & 3 \\ \cos{t} & \sin{t} & 0 \end{array} \\[5pt] & = \ \begin{array}{|cc|} -\cos{t} & 3 \\ \sin{t} & 0 \end{array} \, \mathbf{i} - \begin{array}{|cc|} \sin{t} & 3 \\ \cos{t} & 0 \end{array} \, \mathbf{j} + \begin{array}{|cc|} \sin{t} & -\cos{t} \\ \cos{t} & \sin{t} \end{array} \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] & = \left\langle -3\sin{t} , 3\cos{t}, 1 \right\rangle \end{align}

Now, we compute $||\mathbf v||$ and $||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{\left(\sin{t}\right)^2 + \left(-\cos{t}\right)^2 + \left(3\right)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{\sin^2{t} + \cos^2{t} + 9} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{1 + 9} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{10}, \\[7pt] ||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a|| & = \sqrt{\left(-3\sin{t}\right)^2 + \left(3\cos{t}\right)^2 + \left(1\right)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{9\sin^2{t} + 9\cos^2{t} + 1} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{9\left(\sin^2{t} + \cos^2{t}\right) + 1} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{9 + 1} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{10} \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_N &= \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{10}} \\[5pt] & = 1. \end{align}

question.text: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t > 0$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) = \left\langle 0, \, t, \, 2t^2 \right\rangle.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.explanation:
The normal component of acceleration is given by \[ a_N = \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(0\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(t\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(2t^2\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle 0, \, 1,\, 4t \rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \times \mathbf a{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v \times \mathbf a & = \left\langle 0, \, t, \, 2t^2 \right\rangle \times \langle 0, \, 1,\, 4t \rangle \\[5pt] & = \begin{array}{|ccc|} \mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 0 & t & 2t^2 \\ 0 & 1 & 4t \end{array} \\[5pt] & = \ \begin{array}{|cc|} t & 2t^2 \\ 1 & 4t \end{array} \, \mathbf{i} - \begin{array}{|cc|} 0 & 2t^2 \\ 0 & 4t \end{array} \, \mathbf{j} + \begin{array}{|cc|} 0 & t \\ 0 & 1 \end{array} \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 2t^2 , 0, 0 \right\rangle \end{align}

Now, we compute $||\mathbf v||$ and $||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} ||\mathbf v|| & = \sqrt{\left(0\right)^2 + \left(t\right)^2 + \left(2t^2\right)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{4t^4 + t^2}, \\[3pt] & = t\sqrt{4t^2 + 1},\\[7pt] ||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a|| & = \sqrt{\left(2t^2\right)^2 + \left(0\right)^2 + \left(0\right)^2} \\[3pt] % & = \sqrt{4t^4} \\[3pt] & = 2t^2 \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get \begin{align} a_N &= \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2t^2}{t\sqrt{4t^2 + 1}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2t}{\sqrt{4t^2 + 1}}. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating Components of Acceleration at a Particular Moment

question.text: The velocity $\mathbf v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf {v}(t) = \left\langle -t^2, \, 1,\, t \right\rangle.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t = 1 \, \textrm s.$
question.explanation:
The normal component of acceleration is given by \[ a_N = \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we evaluate $\mathbf v(1){:}$ \[ \mathbf v(1) = \langle -1, \, 1,\, 1 \rangle \]

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t = 1,$ as follows: \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( -t^2 \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 1 \right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( t \right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle -2t , \, 0 , \, 1 \right\rangle, \\[7pt] \mathbf a(1) & = \left\langle -2 , \, 0 , \, 1 \right\rangle \end{align}

Then, we compute $\mathbf v(1) \times \mathbf a(1), ||\mathbf v(1)||,$ and $||\mathbf v(1) \times \mathbf a(1)|| {:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v(1) \times \mathbf a(1) & = \langle -1, \, 1, \, 1 \rangle \times \left\langle -2, \, 0, \, 1 \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \begin{array}{|ccc|} \mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\[0pt] -2 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \\[5pt] & = \begin{array}{|cc|} 1 & 1 \\[0pt] 0 & 1 \end{array} \, \mathbf{i} - \begin{array}{|cc|} -1 & 1 \\[0pt] -2 & 1 \end{array} \, \mathbf{j} + \begin{array}{|cc|} -1 & 1 \\[0pt] -2 & 0 \end{array} \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 1 , -1, 2 \right\rangle, \\[7pt] ||\mathbf v(1)|| & = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 1^2 + 1^2}\\[3pt] & = \sqrt{3}, \\[7pt] ||\mathbf v(1) \times \mathbf a(1)|| & = \sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2 + 2^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt 6 \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t= 1,$ and we get \begin{align} a_N &= \dfrac{||\mathbf v(1) \times \mathbf a(1)||}{||\mathbf v(1)||} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ \sqrt 6}{\sqrt{3}} \\[5pt] & = \sqrt{2}. \end{align}

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is $\sqrt{2} \, \textrm{ms}^{-2}.$

example.title: Calculating Components of Acceleration at a Particular Moment

question.text: The position $\mathbf r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)= \left\langle -t, \, 1, \, t^2 \right\rangle,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t = 1 \,\textrm s.$
question.explanation:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by \[ a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t = 1,$ as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf v & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-t\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(1\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(t^2\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle -1, \, 0 , \, 2t \rangle,\\[7pt] \mathbf v(1) & = \langle -1, \, 0, \, 2(1) \rangle \\[3pt] & = \langle -1 , \, 0, \, 2 \rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t = 1{:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-1\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(0\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(2t\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle 0, \, 0,\, 2 \rangle, \\[7pt] \mathbf a(1) & = \langle 0, \, 0, \, 2 \rangle \end{align}

Then, we compute $\mathbf v(1) \cdot \mathbf a(1)$ and $||\mathbf v(1)||\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf v(1) \cdot \mathbf a(1) & = \langle -1, \, 0,\, 2 \rangle \cdot \langle 0, \, 0,\, 2\rangle \\[3pt] & = 4, \\[7pt] ||\mathbf v(1)|| & = \sqrt{ (-1)^2 + (0)^2 + (2)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{5} \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t = 1,$ and we get \begin{align} a_T & = \dfrac{\mathbf v(1) \cdot \mathbf a(1)}{||\mathbf v(1)||} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{5}. \end{align}

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{5} \,\textrm{ms}^{-2}.$

question.text: The position $\mathbf r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)= \langle \sqrt{2}t, \, t,\, t^3 \rangle,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\textrm s.$
question.explanation:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by \[ a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf v & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(t), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(t^3) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle \sqrt{2}, \, 1,\, 3t^2 \rangle\\[5pt] \mathbf v(1) & = \langle \sqrt{2}, \, 1,\, 3(1)^2 \rangle \\[3pt] &= \langle \sqrt{2}, \, 1,\, 3 \rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=1$: \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(\sqrt{2}), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(1), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(3t^2) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle 0, \, 0,\, 6t \rangle \\[7pt] \mathbf a(1) & = \langle 0, \, 0,\, 6(1) \rangle \\[3pt] &= \langle 0, \, 0,\, 6\rangle. \end{align}

Then, we compute $\mathbf v(1) \cdot \mathbf a(1)$ and $||\mathbf v(1)||\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v(1) \cdot \mathbf a(1) & = \langle \sqrt{2}, \, 1,\, 3 \rangle \cdot \langle 0, \, 0,\, 6\rangle \\[3pt] & = 18 \\[6pt] ||\mathbf v(1)|| & = \sqrt{ (\sqrt{2})^2 + 1^2 + 3^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{12}\\[3pt] & = 2\sqrt{3} \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=1$, and we get \begin{align} a_T & = \dfrac{\mathbf v(1) \cdot \mathbf a(1)}{||\mathbf v(1)||} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{18}{2\sqrt{3}}\\[5pt] &= 3\sqrt{3}. \end{align}

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $3\sqrt{3}\,\textrm{ms}^{-2}.$

example.title: Calculating Components of Acceleration at a Particular Moment

question.text: The position $\mathbf r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)= \left\langle \cos{t}, \, -\sin{t}, \, t \right\rangle,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t = \pi \,\textrm s.$
question.explanation:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by \[ a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t = \pi,$ as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf v & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(\cos{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-\sin{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(t\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle -\sin{t}, \, -\cos{t} , \, 1 \rangle,\\[7pt] \mathbf v(\pi) & = \langle -\sin{\pi}, \, -\cos{\pi}, \, 1 \rangle \\[3pt] & = \langle 0 , \, 1,\, 1 \rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t = \pi{:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-\sin{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-\cos{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(1\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle -\cos{t}, \, \sin{t},\, 0 \rangle, \\[7pt] \mathbf a(\pi) & = \langle -\cos{\pi}, \, \sin{\pi}, \, 0 \rangle \\[3pt] & = \langle 1, \, 0,\, 0\rangle \end{align}

Then, we compute $\mathbf v(\pi) \cdot \mathbf a(\pi)$ and $||\mathbf v(\pi)||\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf v(\pi) \cdot \mathbf a(\pi) & = \langle 0, \, 1,\, 1 \rangle \cdot \langle 1, \, 0,\, 0\rangle \\[3pt] & = 0, \\[7pt] ||\mathbf v(\pi)|| & = \sqrt{ (0)^2 + (1)^2 + (1)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{2} \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=\pi,$ and we get \begin{align} a_T & = \dfrac{\mathbf v(\pi) \cdot \mathbf a(\pi)}{||\mathbf v(\pi)||} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{0}{\sqrt{2}}\\[5pt] &= 0. \end{align}

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $0 \,\textrm{ms}^{-2}.$

example.title: Calculating Components of Acceleration at a Particular Moment

question.text: The position $\mathbf r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)= \left\langle e^{t}, \, -te^{t}, \, 2t \right\rangle,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t = 0 \,\textrm s.$
question.explanation:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by \[ a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}. \]

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t = 0,$ as follows: \[ \begin{align} \mathbf v & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(e^{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-te^{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left( 2t \right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle e^{t}, \, -(t+1)e^{t} , \, 2 \rangle,\\[7pt] \mathbf v(0) & = \langle e^{0}, \, -(0+1)e^{0}, \, 2 \rangle \\[3pt] & = \langle 1 , \, -1, \, 2 \rangle \end{align} \]

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t = 0{:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf a & = \left \langle \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(e^{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-(t+1)e^{t}\right), \, \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(2\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \langle e^{t}, \, -(t+2)e^{t},\, 0 \rangle , \\[7pt] \mathbf a(0) & = \langle e^{0}, \, -(0+2)e^{0}, \, 0 \rangle \\[3pt] & = \langle 1, \, -2, \, 0 \rangle \end{align}

Then, we compute $\mathbf v(0) \cdot \mathbf a(0)$ and $||\mathbf v(0)||\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf v(0) \cdot \mathbf a(0) & = \langle 1, \, -1,\, 2 \rangle \cdot \langle 1, \, -2,\, 0\rangle \\[3pt] & = 3,\\[7pt] ||\mathbf v(0)|| & = \sqrt{ (1)^2 + (-1)^2 + (2)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{6} \end{align}

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t = 0,$ and we get \begin{align} a_T & = \dfrac{\mathbf v(0) \cdot \mathbf a(0)}{||\mathbf v(0)||} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6}}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}. \end{align}

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2} \,\textrm{ms}^{-2}.$
